correctness.rationale: For z=(a,bx) with a≥0, b=(1-a^p)^(1/p), x a Daugavet point in Y, every slice of ℝ⊕pY contains an almost norming radial pair (u0,r) and a Y-witness nearly distance 2 from x. Minkowski and (b+r)^p≥b^p+r^p force dc≥[(1-a)^p+b^p]^(1/p); scalar-axis slices u→1 attain the upper bound. Any slice containing z also contains (a,bw) for w in a suitable Y-slice far from x, hence δc≥2b. Scalar slices u>a-η provide the reverse bound: H(u)=(u-a)^p+(b+(1-u^p)^(1/p))^p decreases for u≥a, and the short interval u<a converges to H(a)=(2b)^p. Endpoints a=0,1 treated separately. Independently checked H at 2,000 mesh points for p=1.5,2,4 with a=.4 and confirmed exact maximum (2b)^p, a finite diagnostic. The strict gap dc<δc for a<1 follows from (1-a)^p<1-a^p and 2<2^p. The whole-space Delta-point locus requires Y to have Daugavet property; selected-point profile only needs x to be a Daugavet point.
